stem: A harvest decision is based on one close-up image from a single upper flower. What is the strongest methodological weakness?
choices: A single upper-flower image may not represent maturity across other flowers, plants, or canopy positions
A close-up image provides useful visual detail but should generally be given more weight than plant identity or sampling location
An upper flower is a reasonable reference point when it receives strong light, even when lower-canopy development has not been sampled
A single image can support harvest timing if the cultivar's expected flowering duration is documented in the same record
rationale: Maturity can vary by plant age, genotype, flower, and canopy position. A single image should not substitute for representative repeated observations.
